kevin: Heads-up — after today's deploy of sysprompt v3 we see an ~8% drop in prefix cache hit rate on p95 traffic. Deployed at 11:05 UTC. Anyone else seeing this?

anita: Yea noticed more cold starts for chat-route-alpha. Latency spike aligns with deploy window. :grimacing:

sara: grabbing profiler traces now. Sending quick summary in a sec.

perf-bot: [auto] prefix-cache-report: route=chat-alpha, window=11:00-11:30, hit_rate_before=0.87, hit_rate_after=0.80, delta=-0.07

kevin: Thanks perf-bot. Sara — if you can paste root cause that'd be great. My suspicion: sysprompt v3 added a new function/metadata blob and we might be including it verbatim in the cache key.

sara: Quick notes from heap/profile:
- The cache key fingerprint now often contains the entire sysprompt block for some requests.
- Kernel selection shifted for these requests: many moved from the multi-token fast path to the per-token fallback kernel because sequence-length distribution changed after normalization.
- Batching heuristics ended up creating smaller micro-batches (~1-2 requests) for that cohort which amplified KV warmup cost.

mike: Can you dump an example cache key? would like to see how sysprompt appears in it.

sara: example (redacted):
```
prefix_sig=v1|tokver=14|model=gptx|sys="Assistant: You are a helpful agent. [tools: [{name:\"search\",schema: {...}}]]"|prompt_hash=0xab12
```

anita: oof — that sys field is huge and includes unordered tool array. If tool ordering isn't stable, identical logical prompts hash different keys.

kevin: So two issues: (1) we're including system content plus tool metadata in the key without normalization; (2) tokenizer/version pinning isn't consistent so the same text tokenizes differently across hosts. Both can fragment cache.

ops: Flagging rollout and start rollback discussion if throughput doesn't recover by EOD.

kevin: Proposal: immediate mitigation steps — roll back sysprompt change to v2 on chat-alpha, and in parallel push a short-term key-normalizer on the runtime to: strip insignificant whitespace, sort tool entries by name, and append tokenizer_version to the key seed. Thoughts?

mike: Sorting tool entries + tokenizer_version append sounds low-risk. We should also special-case system prompts behind an opt-in flag: allow customers to mark "ignore_for_cache" so infra omits that field from the signature.

anita: Agree. For rollout: we can ship key-normalizer as a binary toggle on the serving tier (no model code change) — should be safe. But watch for semantic changes: some customers rely on system prompt differences intentionally. Need a per-tenant opt-out.

sara: Also: kernel selection/batching interplay — when keys fragment, cold-KV misses cause many single-token warmups which trigger the fallback kernel. That explains the latency tail even without huge CPU change. Suggest adding a micro-batching policy: if a request's prefix was cold but similar tokens are queued within 50ms, hold 2-3ms to coalesce. Low-risk and can improve kernel utilization.

kevin: Nice. So immediate action items:
1) Toggle key-normalizer (sort tool array, strip whitespace, include tokeniser_version).
2) Add per-tenant sysprompt cache-exclude flag for Private/Dedicated customers.
3) Short batch-hold heuristic: 2-3ms coalesce window for likely-warmup cohorts.
4) If no improvement in 30m, rollback sysprompt v3 on chat-alpha.

perf-bot: [auto] queued job created: job_id=pc-9921, action=compute-impact-estimate, window=11:00-11:45

mike: For (1) implement normalization code like:
```
normalize_key(parts):
  parts.sys = normalize_whitespace(parts.sys)
  parts.tools = sorted(parts.tools, key=lambda t: t.name)
  parts.tokenizer = parts.tokenizer + "-v" + tokenizer_version
  return hash(concat(parts))
```
Keep as toggle behind env var.

anita: Also run abtest: enable key-normalizer for 10% of traffic on chat-alpha first, track prefix-hit-rate/p95.

sara: I'll wire the profiler to tag requests by cohort and capture kernel path & batch-size distribution for the experiment.

kevin: Great. Assign owners? Sara for profiling + rollout metric dashboards. Mike for key-normalizer. Anita for rollout gating and tenant opt-out logic. Ops to monitor and be ready to rollback.

ops: ACK. Monitoring alerts: added temporary alert if p95 latency delta > +60ms or prefix hit delta <-3% for chat-alpha.

mike: I'll push a PR with toggle and tests in ~30m.

sara: Posting back with first profiler dump in 20m.

kevin: Thanks team — let's keep replies short and only update if you have blockers. :thumbsup:
